newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ATHLETICS-KIPTANUI RUNS THIRD FASTEST STEEPLECHASE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPTANUI RUNS THIRD FASTEST STEEPLECHASE.

text.p: Moses Kiptanui failed in a valiant bid to break his world 3,000 metres steeplechase record on Monday but still recorded the third fastest time ever.
After following two fellow-Kenyan pacemakers through the first 2,000 in world record pace at the Stockholm Grand Prix, Kiptanui set off on his own.
He went through the bell in six minutes 58 seconds but could not quite maintain the momentum on the final lap, clocking eight minutes 01.80 seconds.
Kiptanui, who set his world mark of 7:59.18 in Zurich two years ago, is the only man to have run faster.

Trinidad's Ato Boldon, relishing the fine, hot weather cast off some recent indifferent form to win the men's 100 metres in a meeting record 9.95 seconds and was rewarded with a diamond valued at $10,000.

The impressive American 100 champion Marion Jones took the women's 200 in 22.16, fastest time in the world this year and Britain's Kelly Holmes, the world bronze medallist, won the women's 800 in 1:57.14, also a year's best.
"It was my toughest race of the year," Holmes said.
"I haven't raced seriously over the distance. However, it showed how strong I am and I am certainly considering running both the 800 and the 1,500 at the Athens world championships."
Olympic and world high hurdles champion Allen Johnson opted for the 200, winning in a personal best 20.26.
